record.question: A drug can be called an agonist:
options: If it binds to a receptor and causes opposite effect.
If it binds to a receptor and blocks the receptor.
If it binds to a receptor and produces the intended effect.
If it binds to a receptor and does not produce any effect.
record.explanation: Answer C: If it binds to a receptor and produces the intended effect.. An agonist binds to a receptor and activates it to produce a biological response; “intended effect” is not required for the pharmacological definition. Reference: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK557744/. Verified worked solution, unofficial. Original printed wording and option order reviewed; no matching examiner key is asserted.
